title: A self-driving laboratory discovers lens-and-grating patterns that steer spontaneous emission
summary: A self-driving nanophotonics experiment discovered that combining lens-like refractive-index curvature with grating-like spatial gradient can steer incoherent light emission from a semiconductor metasurface beyond conventional momentum-matching designs. Across a 74° field of view, optimized patterns produced average peak directivity 2.2 times that of sawtooth-grating controls, reaching 67% peak directivity; a fitted equation learner extracted a compact relationship from the experiments.
ai_technology: Variational autoencoder, active-learning experimental planner and neural-network equation learner

evidence.tested: A self-driving nanophotonics experiment discovered that combining lens-like refractive-index curvature with grating-like spatial gradient can steer incoherent light emission from a semiconductor metasurface beyond conventional momentum-matching designs.
evidence.unknown: The article reports local optima under a finite experiment budget, not a global optimum. Measurements were made on a specific GaAs/InAs quantum-dot metasurface; extensions to other emitters or devices remain untested in this study.
evidence.ai_role: The VAE generated pump-pattern configurations, an active-learning agent selected closed-loop physical experiments using measured photoluminescence, and an equation-learning network distilled observed structure–property relationships. The experimental setup measured and human researchers interpreted the results.
